messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] significance of detected QTL and lod interval of fitqtl
messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] significance of detected QTL and lod interval of fitqtl
messages.body_plain:
I'm unfortunately not really able to answer either of your questions.

Regarding assessing significance of QTL in the output of fitqtl, you
don't want to take
the p-values at face value, as you need to take account of the scan
for loci.  I do think
that the application of the permutation threshold you get from a one-
dimensional scan will
be reasonable, but this has not been well proven.

Regarding confidence intervals for QTL location in the context of a
multiple-QTL model,
this has not been well studied.  Probably 1.5-LOD support intervals
are not too bad.  Ideally,
these would be calculated taking into account the uncertainty of the
locations of other QTL,
but this would be quite difficult to calculate.  I think what has
usually been done is to
consider the profile LOD curve of each QTL, keeping the positions of
all other QTL fixed
at their estimated locations.

karl

Hi,
Sorry to return to the problem of mapping with recombinant inbred
lines, but I am having trouble. Using class(myx)[1] <- "riself"  does
not seem to get me the expected change in map length:

> test<-read.cross("csv",,"simple_test.csv",genotypes=c("A","B"))
 --Read the following data:
         100  individuals
         3  markers
         1  phenotypes
> summary(test)
    Backcross

    No. individuals:    100

    No. phenotypes:     1
    Percent phenotyped: 100

    No. chromosomes:    1
        Autosomes:      1

    Total markers:      3
    No. markers:        3
    Percent genotyped:  100

> pull.map(test)
      M1       M2       M3
0.0	10.10135 20.20270
> est.map(test)
      M1       M2       M3
 0.00000 11.14730 22.29460
attr(,"loglik")

> class(test)[1] <- "riself"

    No. phenotypes:     1

        Autosomes:      1

 0.00000 10.10135 20.20270
> est.map(test)
       M1        M2        M3
 0.000000  5.883665 11.767329
attr(,"loglik")
[1] -134.3392
>

What am I doing wrong? It seems that the change in population type is
recognised, but has no immediate effect on the map length. The
existing map is therefore used in QTL mapping. I suppose I could
replace the existing map with the expanded map estimated within R/QTL,
but that isn't the same thing as expanding the given map. Would a
suitable alternative be to expand the map outside R/QTL using  r = 2R/
(1=2R), use this in the input file and then treat the population as a
backcross.

Thanks
Ian

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] another question about using inbred lines
messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] another question about using inbred lines
messages.body_plain:
Dear Ian,

Whether the cross is treated as a backcross ("bc") or RIL by selfing
("riself"),
in the est.map function, we seek to estimate recombination fractions
between markers
(using a multipoint algorithm).  If the cross type is "riself", these
recombination
fractions are then contracted using r' = (r/2) / (1-r).  Then in
either case these
are converted to genetic distances using a map function (by default,
the Haldane
map function is used).

In the calculation of QTL genotype probabilities (given the marker
data) for
use in interval mapping, the genetic distances get converted back to
recombination
fractions using a map function, and, for the cross type "riself",
these recombination
fractions are expanded using R = (2r)/(1+2r).

If you use the map estimated from the data (via est.map), the QTL
mapping results will
be the same, whether you'd used cross type "bc" or "riself".  The
only difference is that,
with cross type "riself" the map will be approximately that
corresponding to meiosis,
while if you used cross type "bc" the map would be expanded by about 2x.

You can see that in your results below.  est.map delivers a map that
is 22 cM long
when you have cross type "bc", and one that is 12 cM long when you
use cross type "riself".

Changing the cross type doesn't change the internal map within the
object.  You need to
use est.map and then replace.map to do that, and you'd want to run
those after you change
the cross type.

karl

messages.subject: singular matricex using cim()
messages.body_plain:
Dear Karl,

I have been using R/qtl for mapping and found a error that happened
some times. I use RILs with a dense genetic map. Using different
phenotypes with the same mapping population I get the error in some of
the cases, so I imagine that the population and marker data is fine.
Also, they work well for interval mapping and for other mapping using
either qtl_cartographer or R/qtlbim. Interestingly, I rerun the same
commands for a couple of phenotypes and got two distinct results: in
some I did not see the error and all the mapping went ok, but in most
of the cases the error appeared again. I also tried changing the
window value for cim but id did not work either.

It seems to me that the error occurs in the execution of the cim()
function. The proccess is generating singular matrices. The plot
resulting of the cim() analysis is a flat QTL line with very high LOD
score (e.g. ~48) and one or two spikes towards more normal LOD score
values.

I would like to know if you have seen this error before and/or know
how to solve it. I would gladly help in any checking that you think
might be useful to troubleshoot this.

Thank you

Bellow I added the relevant commands and output:

R> library(qtl)
R> d = read.cross('qtlcart', file = 'qtlcart.cro', mapfile =
'qtlcart.map')
R> d1 = calc.genoprob(d, error.prob = 0.001, map.function = 'haldane')

... other mapping commands using interval mapping

R> cim = cim(d1, pheno.col = i, window = 10, method = 'em', error.prob
= 0.0001, map.function = 'haldane')
There were 50 or more warnings (use warnings() to see the first 50)
R> warnings();
Warning messages:
1: In checkcovar(cross, pheno.col, addcovar, intcovar,
perm.strata,  ... :
addcovar appears to be over-specified; consider dropping columns.

2: X'X matrix is singular.
3: X'X matrix is singular.

... and the same message goes up to:

49: X'X matrix is singular.
50: X'X matrix is singular.
